title: Bacteriophage Therapy for Staphylococcus Lugdunensis Prosthetic Joint Infection
official: Bacteriophage Therapy for Staphylococcus Lugdunensis Prosthetic Joint Infection
summary: This is a single-patient, phase I/II clinical trial that aims to evaluate the potential of a bacteriophage drug product to treat and prevent the recurrence of a Staphylococcus lugdunensis prosthetic joint infection of the hip. The patient has exhausted all conventional therapies, both surgical and medical, at considerable detriment to their quality of life. The treatment involves 2 intra-articular injections of bacteriophages into the joint and surrounding area and 14 days of intravenous phage therapy. The goal is to eliminate the infection and prevent further complications, providing a potential new treatment avenue for patients with difficult-to-treat infections.

interventions.name: Five phage anti-Staphylococcus aureus bacteriophage cocktail

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of active chronic prosthetic joint infection
* Causative bacteria is susceptible to bacteriophage therapy in vitro
* History of multiple failed antibiotic and surgical interventions

Exclusion Criteria:

* Stage 5 chronic kidney disease
* Cirrhosis
* A known allergy to phage products
* Fever
* Involvement in another clinical trial
* Pregnancy
